sections.h2: Where is New Lenox and how did the village grow?
sections.html:
New Lenox is a village in central Will County, about 36 miles southwest of downtown Chicago. Joliet lies to the northwest, Mokena to the east, Frankfort to the southeast and Manhattan to the south, and the village covers about 15.7 square miles of land.

Fur traders set up an outpost on Hickory Creek in 1829, and the Rock Island Railroad's arrival in 1852 turned the area from farm country into a rail town. The village was platted in 1858 and took the name New Lenox in 1863, after Lenox, New York. It was incorporated on October 4, 1946.

The census count was 1,235 in 1950, 9,627 in 1990 and 17,771 in 2000. It reached 27,214 in 2020, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 28,893, a gain of 6.1% over the April 2020 base. Growth on that scale means many sellers here own houses built from the 1990s onward.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about New Lenox homeowners?
sections.html:
New Lenox is overwhelmingly a place of owned, family-sized houses. These are the Census Bureau's QuickFacts figures for 2020 to 2024:

MeasureNew Lenox
Owner-occupied housing unit rate92.4%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$399,900
Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage$2,700
Median gross rent$1,431
Households9,134
Persons per household3.05
Median household income$140,865

Other figures from the same source: 30.0% of residents are under 18, 95.0% lived in the same house a year earlier, and the mean trip to work is 32.7 minutes. With a trip that long, the Metra station and the I-80 and I-355 ramps are the first things a commuting buyer looks up.

sections.h2: Which New Lenox projects need a village permit?
sections.html:
Most of them do. The Village says permits are required for most construction and homeowner projects, including sheds, decks, pools, fences, roofs, lawn irrigation, siding, window replacement, room additions and basement remodels. Homeowners may do the work themselves, but any contractor must be registered with the Village before the permit is issued.

  • The minimum building permit fee is $75.00. Fees for garages, remodeling, room additions and in-ground pools depend on project cost.
  • Small jobs such as fences, sheds, driveways, roofs and windows can be reviewed over the counter and issued the same day if the application is accurate. Larger reviews can take up to two weeks.
  • Online applications are accepted for furnaces, water heaters, air conditioners, demolition, driveways, electrical upgrades, fences, generators, irrigation systems, roofs, rooftop solar, sewer repairs, and window, door and siding replacement.
  • Online applicants should hear a status within two business days, and no work may begin until the permit is paid for and issued.

The Village's list of miscellaneous permits says private sidewalks, concrete or paver patios, dog runs and playhouses under 100 square feet do not need one. The Community Development Department answers questions at 815-462-6490, and Village Hall at 1 Veterans Parkway is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 5 pm.

sections.h2: How do inspections and winter rules affect a New Lenox sale?
sections.html:
If a permit was never closed out, the Village's inspection steps apply. The Village asks for 48 hours of notice for building inspections and 24 hours for water meter and plumbing inspections, and it charges a fee for a failed inspection, including one where the work is not ready when the inspector arrives.

Winter adds a second limit. From December 1 through March 30 the Village prohibits placing concrete flatwork, and it regulates timing and insulation for footings and foundations. Bonds are accepted in place of exterior concrete during those months. A seller with an unfinished driveway apron or public walk should ask the Building Department how that bond works before a closing date is set.

The Village also keeps a Vacant Property Registration form on its permits page. If the house will sit empty during a sale, ask Community Development whether that registration applies to you.

sections.h2: What does the Will County Recorder require for a New Lenox deed?
sections.html:
New Lenox deeds record with the Will County Recorder of Deeds at 158 N. Scott Street in Joliet, phone 815-740-4637. The fee schedule effective October 1, 2025 lists $90.00 for a standard document and $118.00 for a non-standard one, and the $19.00 Rental Housing Support Program surcharge is part of those totals.

The recorder's deed checklist asks for:

  • The preparer's name and mailing address, and a return address for the document.
  • The permanent index number and a legal description.
  • A notarized original deed, not a copy.
  • The grantee name and address, and the name and address for tax bills.
  • A completed transfer declaration or exemption under the Illinois transfer tax law.

The checklist also lists municipal transfer tax stamps for nine municipalities: Aurora, Bolingbrook, Channahon, Joliet, Naperville, Park Forest, Romeoville, University Park and Woodridge. New Lenox is not on that list. Ask the Village Hall whether any local stamp or payoff step applies to your closing.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and hospitals are close to New Lenox homes?
sections.html:
New Lenox School District 122 runs the elementary and middle schools. High schoolers attend Lincoln-Way Community High School District, which serves New Lenox, Frankfort, Mokena, Manhattan and a small part of Tinley Park. Lincoln-Way Central and Lincoln-Way West are in New Lenox, Lincoln-Way East is in Frankfort, and Providence Catholic High School is also in the village.

U.S. Route 30 is the main east-west road, with Cedar, Gougar and Nelson roads running north and south. I-80 and I-355, the Veterans Memorial Tollway, both pass through. The Metra Rock Island District station is at U.S. 30 and Cedar Road, and a second station at Laraway Road is on the SouthWest Service line.

Silver Cross Hospital moved to a $400 million building off U.S. 6 near the I-355 extension on February 26, 2012.

sections.h2: What does New Lenox weather mean for a house in the listing?
sections.html:
Winters are cold enough to matter. January averages about 21 degrees Fahrenheit, July averages 73, and the village sees on average 137 days with lows at or below freezing and 86 days with highs above 80. Record readings run from 104 degrees down to minus 27.

Those swings are hard on roofs, gutters, driveways, and sump systems in basements. Keep receipts for roof work and the sump pump, since both are standard questions in any sale.

sections.h2: What parks and community amenities do buyers ask about in New Lenox?
sections.html:
The New Lenox Community Park District maintains 40 parks and athletic fields on nearly 600 acres. The 22-mile Old Plank Road Trail passes through the village and reaches Village Hall at the Commons, which opened in 2005 with a performing arts pavilion. The Hickory Creek State Nature Preserve adds a 2.8-mile trail, and the Hadley Valley Preserve has a 4.85-mile crushed-stone greenway trail.

Summer concerts and festivals such as Cruise the Commons and Christmas in the Commons run out of the same civic center.

faqs.q: Do I need a village permit before selling my New Lenox house?
faqs.a: Not to sell, but open permits and unpermitted work can come up in a buyer's review. The Village requires permits for most construction projects, so call Community Development at 815-462-6490 if you remodeled, added a deck or replaced a roof.

faqs.q: Which office records a New Lenox deed?
faqs.a: The Will County Recorder of Deeds in Joliet. Its standard document fee has been $90.00 since October 1, 2025, and the deed must be an original with a notarized signature, a legal description and a permanent index number.

faqs.q: Does New Lenox charge a municipal transfer tax stamp?
faqs.a: The Will County Recorder's deed checklist names nine municipalities that issue transfer stamps, and New Lenox is not among them. Ask Community Development at 815-462-6490 before closing, since that list is the county's summary of what deeds need.

faqs.q: Can I sell a New Lenox house with unfinished concrete work?
faqs.a: Yes, but winter timing matters. The Village bars concrete flatwork from December 1 through March 30 and accepts a bond in place of exterior concrete during that period, so ask the Building Department what the bond requires.

faqs.q: How old are most New Lenox houses?
faqs.a: No single answer fits, but most of the building came between 1990 and 2010. The census count rose from 9,627 in 1990 to 17,771 in 2000 and 24,394 in 2010, so houses from those years are common.
